subject: Post-demo acceptance checklist + proposed eval plan for performance validation
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Turner <ryan.turner@brightpath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T14:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo acceptance checklist + proposed eval plan for performance validation

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the clear framing of BrightPath's performance expectations. I wanted to capture the immediate acceptance criteria we discussed and propose a pragmatic eval plan so we can get you reproducible numbers quickly. High-level recap: 

- Target latency: p95 <= 260ms for typical 128-token responses in streaming mode (aiming for p50 ~ 70–90ms).
- Sustained throughput: 250 qps for the session-level workload (mixed request types, see notes).
- Concurrency: ability to maintain targets with 120 concurrent sessions and 4x KV cache warm-up.
- Streaming requirements: sub-100ms chunking latency and stable token emit while supporting mid-generation cancels.

Attachments: I attached an acceptance checklist and the prompt set we propose to run. Key asks for BrightPath to unblock runs:

1) Access: a whitelisted IP range or temporary test credentials for your staging endpoint (or an S3 bucket with sample telemetry if you prefer runs on our infra).
2) Priority prompt types: telemetry summarization (short), clinical note expansion (long tail), and interactive clarifying-questions (streaming). We included sample distribution percentages in the checklist.
3) Hardware/instance expectations: confirm if staging uses A100/4 or A10-based instances so we align kernel/quantization profiles.

Proposed timeline: deliver reproducible harness + prompt pack by EOD 5/2; run engineer-to-engineer bench on 5/3; share lab report on 5/4. If that works, Ben will own the harness handoff and Markus will coordinate SLO acceptance thresholds.

Next steps I can action now: send the tuned eval_harness_config, and a small script that pins RNG seeds, sequence-length buckets, and warm-up schedule to ensure reproducibility across runs. Please reply with preferred access method and any constraints (e.g., internal PCIe network limits).

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: performance_acceptance_checklist.xlsx (12 KB)]
[Attachment: prompt_set_v2.jsonl (4.2 KB)]
From: Ryan Turner <ryan.turner@brightpath.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightpath.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo acceptance checklist + proposed eval plan for performance validation

Evelyn — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. Quick answers to unblock: 

- Access: we prefer Redwood to run the benchmark against our staging endpoint (we'll provide an allowlist). I'll share a temporary key and allowlist range by EOD today.
- Hardware: staging is on Nvidia A10s for now (we're scheduling A100s later in Q3). Can you run the bench with an A10 profile?
- Prompt mix: confirmed — the distribution in the checklist looks representative.

One additional ask from our platform team: we need the bench to report cold-start tail latency (first-token p99 over 100 cold starts) separately from warm steady-state so we can reason about burst behavior. Also, please include network emulation for 30–80ms RTT to mimic our regional customers.

If you can share the harness and a short run plan, Sarah and I will validate the allowlist and schedule the 5/3 session.

-Ryan
Ryan Turner
Senior Platform Engineer, BrightPath Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Turner <ryan.turner@brightpath.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo acceptance checklist + proposed eval plan for performance validation

Ryan — appreciate the clarity. A few technical clarifications and what we'll instrument on our side: 

- Cold-start: we'll run 150 isolated cold-start trials (container spin + model load + first-token) and report p50/p95/p99. We'll tag those separately in the CSV output and in the dashboard snapshot.
- Warm steady-state: steady-state runs will include 5m warm-up, then 30m measurement windows at target concurrency. We'll report p50/p90/p95/p99 for token-emit and first-token latencies.
- Batching/concurrency: harness will simulate your mixed workload with request-size buckets (seq32/seq128/seq512) and automatic batching. We'll expose batch-size histograms so you can see the correlation to latency.
- Streaming: we'll test chunk sizes you suggested and include mid-generation cancels (10% cancel rate) to validate KV cache cleanup behavior.
- Reproducibility: harness will pin seeds, log the exact container image + sha, CUDA/cuDNN versions, and use a deterministic tokenization snapshot. We'll include a small readme to re-run locally.

I attached the eval_harness_config.yml and a short set of local-run commands. For the A10 profile: we'll use the A100 kernel selection as baseline and fall back to A10-optimized kernels — there may be a small p95 delta but we'll call that out.

Proposed engineer-to-engineer 1-hour window on 2027-05-03 16:00 UTC to run 2x 15-minute steady-state passes (different prompt mixes) + cold-start batch. If that works, please confirm the allowlist + key and we'll kick off at that time.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: eval_harness_config.yml (2.9 KB)]
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Turner <ryan.turner@brightpath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo acceptance checklist + proposed eval plan for performance validation

Ryan / Sarah — thanks for confirming. Quick summary and concrete next steps: 

- Today's deliverables (completed): eval harness config + prompt pack + acceptance checklist (attached). Ben will own run orchestration.
- BrightPath deliverables (requested): staging allowlist + temp key by 5/2 EOD (we received these this morning — thanks). Hardware note accepted (A10).
- Measurement scope to expect in lab report: cold-start p99, warm p50/p95/p99, batch-size distribution, streaming chunk latency, cancel behavior, and a reproducibility section with commands and image SHAs.
- Decision criteria: p95 streaming end-to-end latency <= 260ms and sustained 250 qps at 120 concurrent sessions with <2% error rate. If we meet these, we'll move to an expanded Dedicated sizing run.

Next steps: 1) Ben runs the bench at 2027-05-03 16:00 UTC; 2) Ben uploads lab report to the shared Drive folder; 3) We'll sync on results with BrightPath on 2027-05-04 afternoon (30 min). I'll send a calendar invite after Ben confirms run completion.

Thanks again — looking forward to a reproducible set of numbers.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
